produced_by.server_version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

prng.algorithm: mulberry32 seeded by FNV-1a-32 of the UTF-8 text '<seed>/<purpose>'
prng.next_u32: a = (a + 0x6D2B79F5) mod 2^32; t = a; t = imul(t xor (t >> 15), t or 1); t = t xor (t + imul(t xor (t >> 7), t or 61)); result (t xor (t >> 14)) mod 2^32
prng.randint(lo, hi): lo + floor(next_u32() * (hi - lo + 1) / 2^32), in integer arithmetic

parameters: three balances (100 and two seeded), three amount classes per balance, three levels; amounts on a lattice of 5; the canonical numbers of the executed spikes are fixed inside the grid
history_id: <template>/<pattern>/<cell key>/<level key>/p<permutation index in the cell>
halves: display or graded by the top bit of the first output of the stream seeded by '<seed>/half/<history id>' (ASSESSMENT.md section 2.3 reserves one half of the seed space for worked examples, lesson demonstrations and drawer illustrations)

target.status: [D] design default; the basis is in docs/spikes/W0-S09.md

supply_unit: recorded histories, one per (cell, permutation); presentation variants of one history (names, display order) are not counted. 'distinct_shapes' counts the histories again with the numbers ignored (pattern, levels, permutation), the more conservative measure of how many different problems a learner can meet.
bands: advisory: the band of the first pattern in the order of ASSESSMENT.md section 4.10's table that fits; W4-T20 assigns bands to items

rmw2.title: read-modify-write, two sessions
rmw2.interleavings: every interleaving that cannot hang the tester

cond2.title: conditional UPDATE twin, two sessions
cond2.interleavings: every interleaving that cannot hang the tester

rmw3.title: read-modify-write, three sessions
rmw3.interleavings: a seeded sample of 8 per cell of the valid interleavings

teamsum2.title: team-sum write skew
teamsum2.interleavings: every interleaving that cannot hang the tester

holds2.title: holds write skew
holds2.interleavings: every interleaving that cannot hang the tester

readskew2.title: read skew, two transactions
readskew2.interleavings: every interleaving that cannot hang the tester

readskew3.title: read skew, three transactions
readskew3.interleavings: a seeded sample of 12 per cell of the valid interleavings

readskew2-mixed.title: read skew, mixed isolation levels
readskew2-mixed.interleavings: every interleaving that cannot hang the tester

opposite2.title: opposite-order moves
opposite2.interleavings: every interleaving that cannot hang the tester

ordered2.title: ascending-order moves
ordered2.interleavings: every interleaving that cannot hang the tester

retry-holds.title: attempt log: holds at SERIALIZABLE, failed session retries
retry-holds.interleavings: derived from the recorded histories of holds2: those with one retryable failure and no follow-on error, plus the failed session's retry

retry-cond.title: attempt log: conditional UPDATE, failed session retries
retry-cond.interleavings: derived from the recorded histories of cond2: those with one retryable failure and no follow-on error, plus the failed session's retry

retry-opposite.title: attempt log: opposite-order moves, deadlock victim retries
retry-opposite.interleavings: derived from the recorded histories of opposite2: those with one retryable failure and no follow-on error, plus the failed session's retry

retry-overflow.title: attempt log: a credit past the largest bigint, retried unchanged

retry-unique.title: attempt log: a unique violation, retried blind and retried with a check

history_fields.template: t1 read-modify-write, t2 write skew, t3 read skew, t4 serialization failure or deadlock
history_fields.cell: balance (a string for bigint overflow cells), class, amounts, key
history_fields.permutation: the step order the tester ran, as in its 'starting permutation' line
history_fields.outcome: per session, per transaction: commit, rollback or abort:<SQLSTATE of the first error>
history_fields.waits: steps the tester reported as waiting on a lock
history_fields.errors: every error printed, with step, SQLSTATE and message
history_fields.final: the rows the observer's check step printed last, as printed
history_fields.observed: facts read off the recorded values for the counts: reader totals, team total, held amount
history_fields.block: the tester's output for this permutation, verbatim
history_fields.derived_from_cell: for a retry history, the base cell whose recorded history it extends

cross_listed_for_t4.note: histories in the pools of t1 to t3 whose recorded outcome includes a 40001 or 40P01; a serialization failure shown without a retry is also a t4 instance, and a history shown under one template should count as seen under the others
